thread.title: Tech Today: Spotify Like Netflix, Warming to Roku, Amazon vs. Alibaba - Barron's

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Spotify Like Netflix, Warming to Roku, Amazon vs. Alibaba - Barron's
text:
By Tiernan Ray 11:38 a.m. ET Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Spotify similar to Netflix
Shares of streaming-music pioneer Spotify Technology ( SPOT ) are up $2.25, or 1.4%, at $154.35, after Pivotal Research Group 's Jeffrey Wlodarczak this morning initiated coverage of the stock with a Buy rating and a $200 price target, writing that it is "the clear global leader in premium music streaming," which is important because he thinks "a significant percentage of consumers will move to a subscription streaming all you can eat model for music consumption."
Wlodarczak sees " important similarities " between Spotify and Netflix ( NFLX ), from a product standpoint.
Those similarities include the fact it is subscription-based, it has a "significant underpenetrated opportunity, large investment in tech to create a best in class offering that works on any device," and a "high importance of subscriber growth to increase scale."
Despite that, he does think that there important differences, such as Netflix's investment in "original content," which makes Spotify's opportunity "materially smaller than Netflix."
Netflix’s bright future
Speaking of Netflix, it is no longer the "top pick" at MKM Partners for Rob Sanderson , who now gives that distinction to Alibaba Group Holding ( BABA ). Netflix had been Sanderson’s top pick for the past five years, but now the market is “catching up” to his bullish view, he writes.
Nevertheless, Sanderson this morning raises his price target on Netflix to $390 from $320, writing that the company has "among the very best fundamentals as it joins the internet mega-caps and see an attractive 15% annual return on our current EPS power assumptions."
Netflix stock is up $4.31, or 1%, at $355.60.
Warming to Roku
Shares of another streaming pioneer, Roku ( ROKU ), are down 14 cents at $38.39, despite a somewhat encouraging note this morning from Morgan Stanley ’s Benjamin Swinburne , who raises his rating on the shares to Equal Weight from Underweight, after his concerns about valuation were tempered by this year's 25% drop in Roku’s stock price.
He was concerned prior to this year by the "market overreaction,” he writes, "with shares reaching over 17x '18E platform sales and 12x '19E platform sales (assuming 1.5x fwd player sales)."
But with the stock decline, and the "core fundamentals consistently coming in ahead of our prior expectations (higher ARPU and user growth offsetting lower engagement, see Exhibit 4),” the stock now has a more reasonable valuation, writes Swinburne, "at ~6.5x '19E platform sales as more balanced (below NFLX at ~8x, above Spotify at 3.5x)."
Still, Swinburne is reluctant to recommend the stock, given worries about competition from Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and Alphabet ’s ( GOOGL ) Google unit in the TV platform software war, and also a concern about lack of disclosure of how many hours of viewing on the platform are ad-supported versus subscription-based. It’s critical, he notes, for ad-supported hours of viewing to grow faster than subscription hours.
To achieve that, "Roku needs to negotiate for greater inventory opportunities from partners,” Swinburne writes.
Alibaba vs. Amazon
Speaking of Amazon, Morgan Stanley ’s Brian Nowak and colleagues this morning make the battle of Amazon versus Alibaba the story of the next decade.
 The two companies’ business models, which focus heavily on investments in things such as logistics, are “converging,” the analysts believe.
And with Alibaba’s Chinese market set to be three times larger than that of Amazon’s, Amazon is primed to go head to head with Alibaba in “emerging market battlegrounds."
"We analyze the companies’ efforts to attack the $5tn consumer spend opportunity across India, LATAM, ASEAN, and Australia,” writes Nowak. "For now, we see AMZN ahead in India, BABA ahead in ASEAN, and both players planting seeds in LATAM/Australia.
"From a local perspective, we highlight Flipkart and Snapdeal (in India), Matahari and SEA (in ASEAN) as most exposed to AMZN/BABA disruption risk, with more protected sectors being Consumer and Travel (in India) and FMCG/Tobacco, and Banks (in ASEAN)."
Shares of Amazon are up $1.59 at $1,611.74. Shares of Alibaba are up $1.96, or 1%, at $201.16.
Universal Display jumps on Apple OLED rumor
Among widely circulated tech rumors this morning, India's Economic Times is relating that Apple ( AAPL ) will use organic light-emitting diodes in screens of three different iPhones in 2019, based on a report by Korea’s Electronic Times , which cites multiple unnamed sources from the industry.
That has boosted shares of Universal Display ( OLED ), a supplier of OLED technology that has been in a slump this year as analysts concluded sales of the OLED-based iPhone X were disappointing and that Apple will not extend OLED this year to its other models for the fall lineup.
Shares of Universal are up $5.95, or 6%, at $105.60, though still down 39% for the year so far. Apple stock is down 33 cents at $188.24.
Micron surges
Shares of memory-chip maker Micron Technology ( MU ) are up $2, or 3.4%, at $63.35, on no particular news.
My article in this week’s Barron’s print magazine about artificial intelligence mentioned the company prominently as an important AI chip supplier, and my column in the magazine explored the stock’s stubbornly low valuation.
